sections.h2: The first-timer's checklist: 10 steps from booking to landing
sections.lead: Work through these in order. Each step links to a fuller guide where we have one.
items: Check your passport
It must be valid for at least six months from the date you arrive in India.
Apply for the e-Visa yourself — officially

Only at indianvisaonline.gov.in, at least 4 days before arrival. No agent is needed and the Government charges no express fee. We are not a visa agency. Apply yourself, only at the official site indianvisaonline.gov.in — beware look-alike sites that charge extra. Our e-Visa guide walks through it.
Pick your season
October to March suits Delhi, Agra, Jaipur, Rajasthan, Kerala and Goa. The monsoon usually runs from June to October. See the best time to visit India.
Choose a first route
Delhi, Agra and Jaipur plus one more region is the classic first trip — 10 to 14 days is comfortable. See India in 2 weeks.
Check your arrival airport
The e-Visa works only through designated airports and seaports — check the official list before you buy flights.
Talk to your doctor

Well before you go, see your doctor or a travel clinic, and read CDC (US) or NHS Fit for Travel (UK). A yellow-fever certificate is needed if you arrive from or through a country with yellow-fever risk.
Plan how you'll get around
A private car with driver, reserved trains, or both — booked before you land (see below).
Book key tickets officially
The Taj Mahal is closed on Fridays and opens 30 minutes before sunrise. Buy monument and train tickets only from official sites or counters.
Do your e-Arrival card
Since 1 October 2025, fill in the e-Arrival card within 72 hours before you land, and carry a printout of your e-Visa (ETA).
Read the current travel advice
Check the UK FCDO or US State Department page for India just before you fly — advice changes.
sections.note: Rules and fees change; confirm on the official site before you pay. Visa facts checked on indianvisaonline.gov.in, 18 Oct 2026.

sections.h2: Where to go on your first trip to India
sections.lead: India is a country of many trips. For a first visit, most of our guests choose one of these shapes:
items: The Golden Triangle — Delhi, Agra, Jaipur
The easiest first trip: three cities, short drives, the Taj Mahal at sunrise. Four to six days on its own — see our Golden Triangle tour or a Taj Mahal trip from Delhi.
Golden Triangle + the Himalaya
Our home region: add Shimla, Manali or Dharamshala for mountain air after the plains. See India in 2 weeks.
Golden Triangle + Rajasthan
Forts, palaces and the desert: Jodhpur, Jaisalmer and Udaipur. See our 12-day Rajasthan tour.
The south: Kerala or Goa
Backwaters and tea hills, or beaches — easy to pair with a few days in the north. See our Kerala tour and Goa guide.
A trip around one passion
Yoga in Rishikesh, tigers, or Holi — see yoga retreats, tiger safaris and Holi.
Still deciding?
Browse the best places to visit in India, region by region.

sections.h2: What government travel advice says — and what it means in practice
sections.lead: We quote the official advice word for word, with dates, and add how we plan around it. It is balanced advice for a big country, not a reason to stay away — but read the current version before you travel.
head: Official advice
What it means in practice
rows: US State Department: India is Level 2 – Exercise increased caution “due to crime and terrorism. Some areas have increased risk.” (issued 16 Jun 2025, checked 23 Oct 2026)

Most of the usual first-trip routes are outside the higher-risk areas. Some areas are Level 4 – Do not travel, including Jammu and Kashmir (except eastern Ladakh and Leh), the India–Pakistan border area, parts of central and east India, and Manipur. We tell you plainly if a place you want is affected.
UK FCDO: “Be cautious in tourist areas, where scammers, pickpockets and ticket touts target foreign nationals.” (UK FCDO, page updated 7 Oct 2026)
Keep valuables close in crowds, and buy tickets only from official sites or counters.
UK FCDO: “avoid people at railway stations offering tickets and tours as you may be scammed.”
Book trains online in advance (see below), and politely ignore offers at the station.
UK FCDO: “Avoid travelling at night and in fog as accidents are common due to low visibility.” “Buses are often driven fast and recklessly. Accidents are common.”
We plan daytime drives only, and leave spare time in winter fog and monsoon rain.
UK FCDO: “Avoid travelling alone and hailing taxis on the street, especially at night.” “App-based taxis like Uber and Ola are widely available, including in all airport terminal buildings.”
Use an app taxi or a pre-arranged pick-up, never a street taxi at night. Ask us for a pre-arranged airport pick-up.
UK FCDO: “Be wary of accepting drinks or food from strangers or leaving drinks unattended.”
Keep your drink with you, and eat where you choose.
UK FCDO: “Female travellers often experience verbal and physical harassment by individuals or groups of men.” “Avoid isolated areas, including beaches, when alone at any time of day.”
Women travelling alone or together often prefer a private car and pre-booked hotels. Tell us your concerns and we plan around them.
UK FCDO advises against all travel to Jammu and Kashmir, except air travel to and within Jammu city, and within 10 km of the India–Pakistan border.
Check this before planning Kashmir — see our Gulmarg guide for how we handle it.
sections.note: Sources: UK FCDO India travel advice, safety and security (updated 7 Oct 2026, read 23 Oct 2026); US State Department India travel advisory (issued 16 Jun 2025, checked 23 Oct 2026) — check the current advice before you travel.

sections.h2: Getting around: car with driver, trains and taxis
sections.lead: Distances are long and roads are busy, so first-timers do best with transport booked before they land.
items: Private car with driver

The easiest way for a first trip: the same car and English-speaking driver from the airport to your last day, daytime drives, stops when you want. Your driver's name, photo and car number are shared with you before the trip. See our private car with driver.
Trains

Indian Railways keeps a Foreign Tourist Quota you can book online up to 365 days ahead, with each traveller's passport number and an international card. Other travellers can book only 60 days ahead (since 1 Nov 2024), so the quota helps in busy months.
Taxis in cities
Use app taxis (the FCDO notes Uber and Ola are widely available, including at airports) or a pre-arranged car — not taxis hailed on the street at night.
Mixing both
Many guests take a train for one long leg and a car for the rest. Tell us your route and we suggest the simplest mix.

sections.h2: Money, phones and health: the practical basics
items: Money
Carry an international card and some cash. UPI payment options for visitors exist — check the official NPCI page for current details before you rely on them.
Health

Talk to your doctor or a travel clinic well before you go, and see CDC (US) or NHS Fit for Travel (UK). We don't give medical advice. Most visitors stick to bottled or filtered water — ask your doctor what suits you.
Yellow fever
If you arrive from or through a country with yellow-fever risk, you need a yellow-fever vaccination certificate (official e-Visa site).
Heat and cold
April to June is very hot on the plains, and December–January nights are cold in the north. See the best time to visit India for temperatures by month.

faqs: What should I know before going to India for the first time?

Apply for the e-Visa yourself at indianvisaonline.gov.in at least 4 days before arrival, travel between October and March for the north, keep your first route simple (Delhi, Agra, Jaipur plus one region), travel by day, buy tickets only officially, and book with a registered company on clear deposit terms.
Where should I go on my first trip to India?

Most first-timers start with the Golden Triangle — Delhi, Agra and Jaipur — and add one more region: the Himalayan hill towns, Rajasthan, Kerala or Goa. Our India in 2 weeks itinerary shows how it fits together.
How many days do I need in India?
For a first trip to North India, 10 to 14 days is comfortable: about a week for Delhi, Agra and Jaipur, and the rest for one more region. The Golden Triangle alone takes four to six days.
Is India safe for first-time visitors?

The US State Department rates India Level 2 – Exercise increased caution (issued 16 Jun 2025), with some areas at Level 4. The UK FCDO warns about scammers and touts in tourist areas, and advises avoiding night and fog travel and street taxis at night. We plan daytime drives and pre-arranged transport. Check the current advice before you travel.
How do I get an Indian visa?

Apply yourself, online, only at the official site indianvisaonline.gov.in — beware look-alike sites that charge extra. Apply at least 4 days before arrival with a passport valid for six months. We are not a visa agency; our e-Visa guide explains each step.
What is the best time to visit India for the first time?
October to March, when Delhi, Agra, Jaipur and Rajasthan are dry and mild and Kerala and Goa are in season. The monsoon usually runs from June to October.
Should I hire a car and driver or take trains?

Either works, and many guests mix them. A private car with driver is the simplest for a first trip; trains can be booked online up to 365 days ahead under the Foreign Tourist Quota with your passport number.
How do I avoid scams in India?

Apply for your visa only on the official site, buy monument and train tickets only from official sites or counters, ignore offers of tickets and tours at stations (as the UK FCDO advises), use app taxis or pre-arranged cars, and pay a company only against a written quote and clear terms.
